what_happened: Compiled probes against the real CSLib definitions on the fork's own toolchain (lake env lean on a scratchpad file, no .lean written in either tree) confirmed the LAR carrier is a Fintype by inferInstance once Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Perm is imported, that the explicit-data form discharges the existential proof_wanted in one term, and that the chain-indexed Rabin pairs need no Decidable instance. Cost estimate rests on measurement rather than recall.

The cost estimate on record (the fork's own docstring at DA/Conversions.lean:96-111) names a construction -- 'enumerate all accepting sets as Rabin pairs', same state space, 2^|Q| pairs -- that is not merely incomplete but unsound (already refuted by the archived Muller-sufficiency report's two-state example). The actual construction needs a |Q|!*|Q| state-space blowup, so the estimate on record understates both the state space and the proof work.

Guardrail (f) fires partially: the corpus holds the construction (Thomas 1997 Theorem 6.5, full state set / initial state / transitions / acceptance chain) but NOT the proof of its key invariant (Remark 6.6, stated with 'one verifies the following claim'). The single hardest Lean obligation is precisely the step the corpus leaves unproved.
